cells.tense: You are at the desk right now, choosing what this is going to be.
cells.act: hold your shape under the weight
cells.ask: Next thing that presses on you, hold your shape under it — same size, same pacing — and don't bend to fit it.
cells.core:
What you can do, when it's working, is look at something unformed and say what it is going to be. Not force it — choose it. When the choice comes from what's actually here, the whole thing settles. When it comes from somewhere else, people keep one eye on you.

The version of this that lasts is holding what you've decided without tightening around it. Anybody can choose once and stand firm for a day. Endurance is picking a direction and keeping it while conditions push back, and staying reachable while it's under pressure. That's the work: hold the line without going rigid, and stay open to the people living inside what you've made while it holds.
cells.sheetLine: You can look at a mess and say what it is going to be.
cells.verb: to choose a direction and hold it
cells.place: a place where pattern gets set, where workable form is made from what arrives unshaped

cells.tense: You will have decided before anyone has a chance to tell you what they see.
cells.act: draw the whole arrangement you are inside, with yourself marked on it
cells.ask: Draw the whole arrangement you're inside — who and what is in it, where you sit — and leave the drawing alone for a day before you move anything.
cells.core:
The plan is finished in your head before the situation has had a chance to say what it needs. From inside, that feels like being ready. What it costs you is the thing you're actually good at — choosing based on what's here.

You don't have to stop directing. See the shape of what you're directing. Put the whole arrangement on paper — the people, the moving pieces, where you actually stand in it. Looking at it laid out is not tight control; you can let it sit there being true for a while. The plan that comes after is shorter, and it tends to fit the room you're really in.

cells.tense: You had already stopped before this direction was yours to choose.
cells.act: do one thing today the way only you do it, and do not explain it
cells.ask: Do something small your own way — not well, just yours — and don't explain it to anyone.
cells.core:
There's a particular stuckness where you stopped saying 'this, not that', and the days have run on as versions of each other. From inside it looks like patience. From outside, the engine reads as off. It isn't that you can't choose. You stopped trusting that any choice would hold.

Don't grind it back. Bringing force to this stuckness makes it worse. Instead do one thing the way only you do it. Small. Not because it's a system — because it's yours. You'll notice the difference between doing it that way and doing what anyone would have done. When nothing is explained, no one has to be right about it. One thing done as yourself is a direction starting from nothing.

cells.tense: You are steering now, and to hear you tell it, the current is steering you.
cells.act: put your own name on what is already yours
cells.ask: Take something you did this week that you're calling 'the way it goes' — and write your own name next to it.
cells.core:
The story that runs here is that momentum is doing the driving, and the things you actually chose don't come up as choices. Habit reads as the situation. Convenience reads as circumstance. The one holding the pen is not in the account. That isn't modesty. It's credit left unclaimed.

You can't take it back in the abstract. Only one move at a time. Take something you did this week and write your own name beside it. Not a boast — an accurate line in the record. The moment your name is on one real thing, you're back where the direction gets set. The rest doesn't have to change yet. One name is enough to start.
cells.sheetLine: You're steering now, and by your own account the current is.

attempts.check: I claim that people around the Too Much person feel forced, which is a mechanism claim I cannot see from outside. A reader could say the forcing is happening inside the person and nobody else minds — so I keep the description to what is in the person's own hands. The ask survives being wrong: drawing the arrangement still gives the person something they can use even if the forcing never touched anyone but themselves. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'it has already been decided for you' — I have cut it; I don't know what was decided, or by whom, and the cell doesn't need to say.
